story_type: uncrewed cargo capsule docks itself to the space station and splashes down
hook: Nobody was aboard. This capsule flew itself to the space station.
narration: Nobody was aboard this capsule. It flew itself to the space station.
It launched on a Falcon nine from Kennedy Space Center, carrying cargo for NASA.
Nine engines pushed it through max q, the moment of the highest stress on the rocket.
In orbit, Dragon separated and drifted away from the second stage.
To find the station, it uses lidar. Lasers ping off reflectors on the station and tell Dragon its distance and closing speed.
Astronauts watched it the whole way, making sure it stayed inside an invisible cone toward the docking port.
At ten meters out, its alignment was off by less than half a degree.
[short pause] Then contact, and capture, two hundred sixty one miles above Earth.
When it was time to come home, it backed away from the station on its own thrusters.
outcome: Its parachutes opened over the ocean, and the capsule splashed down.
title: Capsule flew itself to the space station
description:
NASA footage of SpaceX Cargo Dragon resupply missions: launch on a Falcon 9 from Kennedy Space Center, an automated approach and docking at the International Space Station, undocking and splashdown.
